Covid on a Cellular Level

By: John Webb | Production

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
We examine the impact of Covid19 on a group of people in Ireland as they come to terms with an existence in isolation.

Unique Selling Point:
With social distancing the new buzzword, what has the impact been on the lives of people facing the same challenges as many in South Africa but in a very different environment? We get a glimpse of a life in isolation of a group of people in various parts of Ireland. We discover they're as confused and uncertain as people in other parts of the world but, like them, finding strength in the things they once considered mundane. This insert will tell those stories against a backdrop of an ever-changing and increasingly concerning global picture. It will - as a show of respect to what people are calling the "new normal" - be shot almost exclusively on cell phone.

Summary:
This is the story of four days and four people. A sports broadcaster, a lawyer, a tour guide, and a charity founder. They have different backgrounds, live in different parts of Ireland and have different ways of coping with adversity. But they are also the same: facing the same onslaught from the same unseen enemy that has put them temporarily out of work,limited their movements and threatened their health. They'll film themselves going about their lives and talking about their fears and, perhaps, hopes. Their stories will be interspersed with the latest news about the virus as it infects more people and claims more lives on each of the four days of filming.

Script:


Upsound: Leo Varadkar STRAP “Taoiseach, Ireland” Start audio under the graphic [06:44 – 06:55] “This is the calm before the storm, before the surge Cut to visuals …so much of so few”
VO: It’s been four days since that speech; 23 since the first case of Covid-19 was confirmed in Ireland, *** but close to five million Irish still await the surge. These are four of them.
VO: This is a glimpse into their lives in the time of the Corona Virus. It’s television in the age of social distancing – filmed exclusively on cell phones over four days.
Link: These aren’t the most troubling stories you’ll have heard – far from it. They’re just the reflections of people on a small island in Europe grappling with this strange, new reality. Perhaps, when you hear them, you’ll think - as I do – that the world seems a much smaller place right now.
ITV Jane Mccluskey: [Full Size Render 00:00:00 – 00:00:17] “I think what’s really frightening about this virus is the speed at which it’s spread… our leaders”
VO: As mother of three, Jane Mccluskey, is speaking, another 651 people have died in Italy - close to five-and-a-half thousand since the start of the outbreak at the end of January. Italy is just a two-hour flight away.
VO: So close and yet so far removed from the immediate challenges facing people here… in this “calm before the storm”.
ITV Jane Mccluskey: [IMG 8355 00:00:25 – 00:00:36] STRAP “Jane McCluskey” “At the moment I’m home-schooling my eldest… it’s pretty challenging”
VO: It’s a challenge in my household, too. With the vegetable garden a welcome distraction, I catch up on the news.
VO: Ireland’s economy is strong right now, but the country is still under-prepared – short of ICU beds, ventilators and testing kits.
VO: It’s time to venture outside. As the public health system ramps up its preparations, other sectors of the economy are grinding to a halt. This 800-year-old castle, now a hotel has been through testing times recently.
Link This place has just started to recover after the financial crisis in 2008 – it was dealt a significant blow back then. Now, 12 years later it’s back to square one.
VO: Like so many other businesses, it’s closed its doors. Of a population of 4.9 million, it’s said close to 150 000 have already lost their jobs in Ireland.
ITV: Connor Morris [114651 – 00:00:39 – 00:00:50] “Then in the space of… shut down”
VO: Not that long ago, Connor Morris was commentating at the Rugby World Cup in Japan. Out of work for the foreseeable future, he’s focussing his efforts elsewhere.
ITV: Connor Morris [00:01:29 – 00:01:49) STRAP “Connor Morris” “So that has been… far, far from normal”
VO: Far from normal is right. Stricter measures are days away but those already in place have had an impact.
ITV: Connor Morris [00:02:50 – 00:03:17] “I notice over the course of the last week… no one’s talking”
VO: While some still ignore the government’s warnings, he’s right: It’s very quiet. I notice it, too, driving through the small towns and villages close to my home.
VO: But there’s something else: Connor had chronic asthma as a child and still medicates. That puts him in the high-risk category; something his GP warned him about.
ITV: Connor Morris [00:01:55 – 00:02:25] “I can honestly say… on my worst enemy.”
VO: Words like that make you thankful for the quiet. Tomorrow, I’ll head to Ireland’s capital, Dublin to see the impact there.
VO: The river Liffey runs through the middle of Dublin. The roads on either side of it are among the busiest in the city. But not today.
VO: While some are still working and some shops are open, things are not as they usually are. It seems the Covid 19 penny has dropped here, too.
VO: Next to the river is one of 41 Covid-19 testing sites set up across the country. Even so, the State is struggling to keep up.
VO: Dublin is home to Fiona Tuomey. This morning, she’s video calling her husband who recently relocated to the middle east for work. [upsound “Bye” and little wave] Her smile reveals the value of conversations like these – now more than ever.
Question: What’s that like talking to him?
ITV: Fiona Tuomey 141539 [00:00:48 – 00:01:06] “It’s always better… that’s all I can say”.
VO: Dig a little deeper, and the extent of her reliance on technology becomes clearer.
ITV Fiona Tuomey STRAP “Fiona Tuomey, Founder: HUGG.ie” 124528 [00:01:05 – 00:01:21] “My husband… no idea, no idea”
VO: Notice the poster of the smiling little girl in the background. That’s Fiona’s youngest daughter, Milly. She died by suicide four years ago. She was just 11.
ITV Fiona Tuomey [00:01:45 – 00:02:07] “Milly was a vibrant… can affect anybody.”
VO: In 2017, Fiona set up a charitable group called HUGG. It’s run by the bereaved for the bereaved who’ve lost someone to suicide – people who will now be robbed of face-to-face support.
Link: If you think Fiona is wallowing in self-pity, you’d be wrong. She’s making the best of a desperate situation and, like many here hasn’t lost her smile.
ITV Jim Wilson [Covid 19 piece 00:00:24 – 00:00:44] “You know it’s a serious… never happened before”
VO: Like Fiona, Jim Wilson, is determined to keep smiling. He’s a wildlife tour guide; like so many now temporarily out of work. So, he’s turned his attentions elsewhere.
ITV Jim Wilson STRAP “Jim Wilson” [Covid 19 piece 00:06:56 – 0007:21] “A lot of us have… a shed we have” CUT [00:07:48 – 00:08:02] So by the time.. just so good”.
VO: But, Jim’s not unaware of the threat posed by the virus – how could he be when there’s very little else covered in the media these days? The internet is awash with graphics showing Covid-19’s relentless march. He’s just refusing to give in to cynicism.
ITV Jim Wilson [00:10:13 – 00:10:31] “Lot of community spirit here… Jim here, goodbye, thank you.”
VO: Or, perhaps, not goodbye but “farewell”.
Ends.
